profile_guidance: Personas and primary jobs vary by workflow. The following are candidate rules, not universally proven truths.

conditional_rules.when: Primary goal is to complete common setup with varying user familiarity
conditional_rules.prefer: Start with essentials while keeping advanced configuration reachable
conditional_rules.because: Reduces required initial decisions without creating dead ends
conditional_rules.unless: Critical inputs or consequences must be exposed before proceeding
conditional_rules.check: First-run completion, failed setup diagnoses, discovery of advanced controls

conditional_rules.when: A user is performing a focused, time-sensitive task
conditional_rules.prefer: Keep secondary controls visually restrained and contextually accessible
conditional_rules.because: Reduces attention competition and unnecessary context switching
conditional_rules.unless: Safety or diagnosis demands continuous visibility
conditional_rules.check: Task time, return-to-task errors, important status missed

conditional_rules.when: A workflow involves potential errors or uncertain system state
conditional_rules.prefer: Show actionable status, recovery paths and diagnostics
conditional_rules.because: Users must understand errors to recover and trust the system
conditional_rules.check: Recovery rate, time to resolution, support requests

conditional_rules.prefer: Preserve an expert path and settings persistence
conditional_rules.because: Simplification should not create irreversible limitations
conditional_rules.unless: Customization undermines nonnegotiable security or policy
conditional_rules.check: Advanced capability task success and later migration cost

known_gaps: No evidence that one developer persona is always primary
Most rules rely on published philosophy rather than measured outcomes
Need more documented design alternatives and direct user findings
No domain-specific accessibility or regulatory certification
